clips.send: Claim. What you want the reader to believe or do. A claim is arguable: a reasonable person could disagree. “School starts at 7:45” is a fact, not a claim. Make it specific: who should do what? “Our school should add a 20-minute recess” beats “Recess is good.”. Strong claims often include a reason: “…because students focus better after a break.”. Starters: “Our school should…”, “It is time to…”, “The best solution is…”. Claim equals what I think + why, in one sentence. A topic (“phones in school”) is not a claim. A claim takes a side.

clips.send: Evidence. Facts, data, examples or expert words that support the claim. Strong evidence is specific (numbers, names, dates), reliable (an expert or careful study) and relevant (it really is about your claim). Weak evidence: one person’s story, an unnamed website, or data that is too old for the question. Introduce it: “According to the CDC, …”, “A 2018 study found that…”. Two pieces of strong evidence beat five weak ones. Specific, Reliable, Relevant: S-R-R. A strong feeling is not evidence. “I really, really believe it” proves nothing.

clips.send: Conclusion. Restate the claim in new words and call to action. Remind the reader of your claim without copying the first sentence. End with what should happen next, or why it matters to the reader. Starters: “In the end…”, “For these reasons…”, “Let’s…”. Echo the claim, add a call to action. A conclusion does not add brand-new evidence.

clips.send: Reasoning. Explains HOW the evidence proves the claim. Evidence does not speak for itself. Reasoning is the bridge: “This matters because…”. Good reasoning connects the evidence to the claim with a rule or cause: rested brains learn more, so a later start helps learning. Circular reasoning just repeats the claim: “School should start later because it should.”. Starters: “This shows that…”, “This matters because…”, “As a result…”. Evidence equals what. Reasoning equals so what? Repeating the evidence in other words is not reasoning. Say why it matters.

clips.send: Rebuttal. Why your claim still wins. A rebuttal answers the counterclaim with evidence or logic: “However, …”. You may admit part of it (a concession), then show why your side still matters more. Insults (“people who think that are clueless”) are not rebuttals; they are ad hominem attacks. Georgia’s grade 8 standard adds the rebuttal to the claim, evidence and counterclaim you already know. “Yes, but…” with proof. “That might be a problem.” is only a concession. A rebuttal must push back.

clips.send: Counterclaim. The other side’s best point, stated fairly. Naming the other side makes you look fair and confident, not weak. Use their strongest point, not a silly version. Turning it into a silly version is called a “straw man”. Starters: “Some people argue that…”, “Critics may say…”, “It is true that…”. Steel-man, don’t straw-man: make their point strong, then beat it. A counterclaim is not switching sides. You return to your claim right after.

clips.send: 推理（Reasoning）。解释论据“怎样”证明论点。论据不会自己说话。推理是一座桥：“这很重要，因为……”。好的推理用一条规律或因果关系把论据和论点连起来：睡足的大脑学得更好，所以晚点上课有助于学习。循环论证只是把论点再说一遍：“学校应该晚点上课，因为它应该晚点上课。”。英文常用：“This shows that…”“This matters because…”“As a result…”。论据回答“是什么”，推理回答“所以呢？”。换个说法重复论据不是推理，要说出它为什么重要。

clips.send: 反驳（Rebuttal）。说明为什么你的论点仍然成立。反驳用论据或逻辑回应反方观点，常用“However, …”开头。你可以先承认对方有一部分道理（让步），再说明为什么你的观点更重要。骂人（“这么想的人都很蠢”）不是反驳，而是人身攻击。佐治亚州八年级标准在论点、论据、反方观点之外，明确要求写反驳。“是的，但是……”，并且拿出证据。“那可能是个问题。”只是让步。反驳一定要回击。

clips.send: 论点（Claim）。你希望读者相信或去做的事。论点必须“可以争论”：讲道理的人也可能不同意。“学校 7:45 上课”是事实，不是论点。要具体：谁应该做什么？“我们学校应该增加 20 分钟课间休息”比“课间休息很好”强得多。有力的论点常常带着理由：“……因为学生休息后更专心。”。英文常用开头：“Our school should…”“It is time to…”“The best solution is…”。论点 等于 我的看法 + 理由，一句话说清。话题（“学校里的手机”）不是论点。论点必须表明立场。

clips.send: 论据（Evidence）。支持论点的事实、数据、例子或专家意见。有力论据要具体（数字、名字、日期）、可靠（专家或严谨的研究）、相关（真的和你的论点有关）。薄弱论据：某一个人的经历、不知名的网站、对这个问题来说太旧的数据。英文引出论据：“According to the CDC, …”“A 2018 study found that…”。两条有力的论据胜过五条薄弱的论据。具体 · 可靠 · 相关。强烈的感受不是论据。“我真的非常相信”什么也证明不了。

clips.send: 结论（Conclusion）。用新的说法重申论点，并呼吁行动。提醒读者你的论点，但不要照抄第一句。最后说明接下来应该做什么，或者它为什么和读者有关。英文常用：“In the end…”“For these reasons…”“Let’s…”。呼应论点，再加一句行动号召。结论部分不再加入全新的论据。

clips.send: 反方观点（Counterclaim）。公正地写出对方最有力的观点。写出反方观点会让你显得公正、自信，而不是软弱。要用对方最有力的观点，不要故意歪曲成可笑的版本，那叫“稻草人谬误”。英文常用：“Some people argue that…”“Critics may say…”“It is true that…”。把对方的观点说强，再去驳倒它。写反方观点不等于改变立场，紧接着你要回到自己的论点。
